rows.exact_frozen_ssc_body: W04b treats complexified four-dimensional spacetime as the common carrier for SL(2,C)_L x SL(2,C)_R and distinguishes Minkowski and Euclidean real forms by different real subgroup conditions rather than by identifying their chiral factors. W04b prints Spin(4,C)=SL(2,C)_L×SL(2,C)_R; its Minkowski real-form embedding is g∈SL(2,C)↦(conjugate(g),g) with conjugation on the FIRST factor, and its Euclidean preserving group is printed Spin(4)=SU(2)_L×SU(2)_R. Do not swap factor order, remove conjugation, add an inverse/adjoint not printed here, or normalize the group presentation. W04b prints the conventional complex vector presentation S_L tensor S_R (equivalently Hom(S_R*,S_L)) and discusses Weyl Wick rotation as analytic continuation in four-complex-dimensional spacetime. Minkowski needs one spinor kind plus its conjugate, whereas the conventional Euclidean continuation requires independent chiral kinds and Dirac-pair introduction. The author's alternative remains a proposal to use only S_R, not a proved equivalence of physical theories.

rows.exact_frozen_ssc_body: W04b uses T=C4, PT=CP3, and projective CP1 data to describe spacetime points and presents the one-complex-dimensional CP1 case as an instructive lower-dimensional real-form/orbit analogue. The author prints T=C4 with complex spacetime points as C2 subspaces, and PT=CP3 after quotienting by nonzero complex scalars; CP1s represent spacetime points. He proposes exploiting the complex dimension-three PT rather than the four-complex-dimensional family of CP1s. The CP1 analogue has an SL(2,C) transitive conformal-sphere action, SU(2) transitive compact real-form action, and finite-dimensional Borel-Weil/Bott representations on holomorphic sections or H1 cohomology.

rows.exact_frozen_ssc_body: In the CP1 analogue W04b uses the three SU(1,1)=SL(2,R) orbits and hyperfunction boundary values to model the relation between holomorphic domains and Lorentzian boundary data. The three CP1 split-real-form orbits are CP1+ upper hemisphere, CP1- lower hemisphere, and the S1 equator. W04b describes infinite-dimensional unitary discrete-series representations on holomorphic line-bundle sections over either open orbit or H1 cohomology. Boundary function spaces admit different choices, with hyperfunctions described as natural rather than uniquely forced. The Cayley transform relates SL(2,R) upper/lower-half-plane and real-axis actions to SU(1,1) CP1 actions; SL(2,Z) is a number-theory subgroup context, not additional twistor structure. Preserve printed SL(2,R)=SU(1,1) without mathematical normalization.

rows.exact_frozen_ssc_body: For the Euclidean real form W04b uses SL(2,H)=Spin(5,1), C4=H2, and the CP3 -> HP1=S4 fibration with CP1 fibers; Wick rotation requires choosing such a Euclidean fibration and its intersection with the Minkowski null geometry. Under C4=H2, the author calls SL(2,H)=Spin(5,1) the Euclidean conformal real form and says it acts transitively on PT. Quaternion multiplication produces CP3 -> HP1=S4 with CP1=S2 fibers; conformally compactified Euclidean S4 points correspond to these fibers. Choosing the Euclidean fibration determines an S3 subset S4 at the Minkowski intersection, and N has a geometric S2 fibration over S3, not just a topological S3 times S2. The author defers the physics implementation to a later post.
